cvEn:
Israel Lutati, son of Rachel and Eli, was born on 4 Adar II 5744 (8 March 1984) in Netivot. He had a brother, Arnit, and two sisters, Shirel and Daniel. When he was seven, the family moved to the community of Neve Dekalim in the Gush Katif bloc. He studied at the elementary school and at the "Neot Katif" middle school. He completed his high school studies at the Yeshiva High School in Kfar Maimon. In his free time he volunteered with Magen David Adom in Netivot. Israel was a devoted volunteer who always wanted to help, and he would spend his vacations volunteering with the "Gaza Coastal Security Center."

When his yeshiva studies ended, on 25 November 2002, Israel enlisted in the IDF and was assigned to the Givati Brigade. His main reason was a wish to protect his home, since the Givati Brigade was stationed in the Gaza Strip, where he lived. About ten days before he fell, Israel was injured in an accident during his military service and suffered terrible pain. He refused to take sick leave, because he knew that taking it would mean another soldier would have to stay on the base in his place. Israel was prepared to give his life for others, for his people, and for the Land of Israel. His whole life was built on helping others and on acts of loving-kindness. Israel was loved by everyone, got along with everyone, loved peace, made peace, and was always a attentive ear for his friends.

On 8 Tishri 5765 (23 September 2004), after one year and ten months of dedicated service, Staff Sergeant Israel Lutati fell in battle at the Morag outpost. He was twenty years old. He was laid to rest in the cemetery in the Gush Katif bloc. He left behind his parents, a brother, three sisters, a brother-in-law, Amnon, and a niece, Shai, who was one month old. His father, Eli, writes about him: "We believe that the legacy Israel left us and the nation as a whole is one of giving, acts of loving-kindness, and love of the Holy Land. These are the three things that characterized him."

In Israel's memory, a grove was planted in the Yatir Forest by the Negev, Yehuda Shoshan, director of Magen David Adom in the Negev, in cooperation with the JNF Dromm Gilat district, during the Tu BiShvat plantings of 5765. Following the "Disengagement" process, Israel was reinterred in the military plot of the cemetery in Nitzan on 25 Menachem Av 5765, after being moved from the Gush Katif bloc.
